Spearman-correlate every feature with a per-sample trait, optionally given covariates

stats_correlate.Rd

Spearman's rank correlation of every feature of a feature-by-sample table with one per-sample trait, with a two-sided p-value, optionally partial given per-sample covariates.

For each feature (row) of the responses table, mzLib's SpearmanCorrelation.Correlate ranks the feature's values and the trait over the samples where both are known, and tests rho = 0, two-sided. With given, SpearmanCorrelation.PartialCorrelate first removes from both sets of ranks what the covariates' ranks explain, as ppcor::pcor.test(method = "spearman") does. mzLib holds both to R's cor.test() and to ppcor 1.1 to 1e-8 relative.

Usage

stats_correlate(responses, trait, given = NULL, timeout = 600)

Arguments

responses

stats_fit's responses table: a TSV with a header row, the feature id first, then one column per sample, named by its header. Blank, NA or NaN is missing. 0 is an observation, ranked like any other value.

trait

A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name (exactly the responses' sample columns, in any order), then ONE value column, whose header names the trait - age, dose, loading. A blank or NA cell leaves that sample out.

given

A TSV of the same shape with one or more covariate columns (batch, run order, loading) to partial out. Leave it NULL for a plain correlation.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Spearman uses ranks only. It needs no log transform, one extreme value cannot drive it, and it finds any relationship that only ever rises (or only ever falls), not just a straight line.

Value

An mzlibr_correlations:

- records, a data.frame with one row per feature in the responses file's order: feature; rho, Spearman's rho (unitless correlation, -1 to 1), ties at their average rank, the partial rho with given; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided against rho = 0 and not adjusted across features - both NA exactly when method is "not_estimable"; n, the complete samples used (samples: response, trait and every covariate finite); has_ties, whether any variable was tied among them (FALSE too when there were too few to rank); and method, "exact" (n <= 9, no ties, plain), "asymptotic" (t on n - 2 df, or n - 2 - k with k covariates kept) or "not_estimable". - responses_file, trait_file and given_file (NA without given), as absolute paths; trait_name, the trait column's header; covariate_names (empty without given); partial, TRUE with given; feature_count features and sample_count samples read; sample_names; missing_count response cells (cells) that were blank, NA or NaN; trait_missing_count, samples with no trait value (samples); given_incomplete_count, samples missing a covariate (samples), NA without given; method_counts, features per method; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: how the p-values were computed and how they differ from R's defaults, plus a count of not_estimable features when there are any.

Against R's cor.test()

For 10 <= n < 1290 without ties, R's cor.test() default is an Edgeworth series (AS 89), which mzLib does not use, so p-values there differ slightly from R's default output; they match cor.test(exact = FALSE). Send records$p_value to stats_adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

Wraps

Wire verb stats correlate. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.correlate.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • SpearmanCorrelation.Correlate in mzLib/StatisticalModels/SpearmanCorrelation.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SpearmanCorrelation.PartialCorrelate in mzLib/StatisticalModels/SpearmanCorrelation.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SpearmanCorrelation.ExactMaxN in mzLib/StatisticalModels/SpearmanCorrelation.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SpearmanResult in mzLib/StatisticalModels/SpearmanCorrelation.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SpearmanPValueMethod in mzLib/StatisticalModels/SpearmanCorrelation.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

responses

path; required. stats fit's responses table. A TSV with a header row: the first column is the feature id (unique, any header) and every other column is one sample, named by its header. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is missing. Only ranks are used, so a monotone transform such as log2 changes nothing; but a 0 is an observation, ranked like any other value, so blank any 0 that means not measured. Blank lines are skipped.

trait

path; required. A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name, then EXACTLY ONE value column, whose header names the trait (for example age or dose). The sample names must be exactly the responses' sample columns, in any order: rows are matched by name. A blank, NA or NaN cell is a sample with no trait value, left out of every feature's correlation.

given

path; default absent. Optional. A TSV with the trait file's shape but one or more covariate columns, each named by its header: per-sample nuisance variables (batch, run order, loading) to partial out. With it, every feature is correlated by PartialCorrelate instead of Correlate. The sample names must be exactly the responses' sample columns; a blank, NA or NaN cell leaves that sample out of every feature's correlation. Absent, the bridge sends none and the correlation is plain.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

responses_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the responses table.

trait_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the trait table.

given_file

string; NA when no --given: the correlation is plain. Absolute path of the covariates table.

trait_name

string; never NA. The trait file's value column header.

covariate_names

string[]; never NA. The --given file's column headers, in order; empty without --given.

partial

bool; never NA. True with --given: rows are partial correlations (PartialCorrelate).

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Feature rows read; the table's row count.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Sample columns read.

sample_names

string[]; never NA. In responses header order, which is the order the trait and covariate rows were put in.

missing_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that were blank, NA or NaN.

trait_missing_count

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with no finite trait value, so in no feature's correlation.

given_incomplete_count

int; in samples; NA when no --given. Samples missing at least one covariate, so in no feature's correlation.

method_counts

map<string,int>; in features; never NA. Features per method: exact, asymptotic, not_estimable.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Equal to feature_count.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per feature, in responses file order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Four static caveats (five with --given), plus one when any feature is not_estimable, with the count.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the responses file's first column.

rho

float; in unitless correlation (-1 to 1); NA when not_estimable (see method). Spearman's rho: Pearson's correlation of the ranks, ties given their average rank. With --given, the partial rho: the correlation of the feature's and the trait's ranks after each is regressed on the covariates' ranks, all ranked over the complete samples.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not_estimable. Two-sided p-value against rho = 0, computed as method says. 0 when rho is exactly -1 or 1 with the asymptotic test. Not adjusted across features.

n

int; in samples; never NA. Complete samples the correlation used: the response, the trait and (with --given) every covariate finite.

has_ties

bool; never NA. Whether any variable (the response, the trait or, with --given, a covariate) has tied values among the complete samples. Also false when there were too few complete samples to rank at all (n below 3, or below 4 with --given), where mzLib does not look.

method

string; never NA. exact (the full permutation distribution of S = sum d^2, for n <= 9 with no ties and no --given, as R's cor.test exact = TRUE) | asymptotic (t = rho sqrt(df / (1 - rho^2)) on df = n - 2, or n - 2 - k for k covariates kept, as cor.test exact = FALSE and ppcor::pcor.test) | not_estimable (fewer than 3 complete samples, or k + 3 with --given; a constant variable; or covariates that carry the response or the trait entirely).

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

responses or trait missing, blank or not found; --given given without a value or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; the trait file with other than exactly one value column; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or column name; a cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the trait's or the covariates' samples are not exactly the responses' sample columns (both differences are named)

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Plain: p_value is exact, from the full permutation distribution, for n <= 9 without ties, as R's cor.test(method = 'spearman'); otherwise it is asymptotic, t with n - 2 degrees of freedom, as cor.test(exact = FALSE).

  • Plain: for 10 <= n < 1290 without ties, R's cor.test default is an Edgeworth series (AS 89), which mzLib does not use, so p-values there differ slightly from R's default output.

  • With --given: every variable is ranked over the samples complete in all of them, rho is the correlation of the feature's and the trait's ranks after each is regressed on the covariates' ranks, and p_value is from t with n - 2 - k degrees of freedom, as ppcor::pcor.test(method = 'spearman'). mzLib drops a covariate that the others carry entirely, and k counts the covariates kept; mzLib does not report k, so neither does this verb.

  • With --given: give only nuisance covariates. A covariate that follows the trait takes the trait's own signal with it.

  • A sample enters a feature's correlation only when its response, its trait and every covariate are finite: missing values are omitted, never imputed. n is the number of samples used.

  • p_value is not adjusted across features. Send the p_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.stats.correlate

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::correlate_with with CorrelateOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_correlate

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

References

  • doi:10.2307/1412159: the rank correlation coefficient rho (Spearman, Am J Psychol 15:72, 1904)

  • doi:10.5351/CSAM.2015.22.6.665: ppcor, whose pcor.test(method = 'spearman') the partial form (--given) reproduces (Kim, Commun Stat Appl Methods 22:665, 2015)

  • doi:10.2307/2347111: the Edgeworth series (AS 89) R's cor.test uses by default for 10 <= n < 1290, which mzLib does NOT use (Best and Roberts, Appl Stat 24:377, 1975)

See also

stats_fit for a linear model on the same responses, stats_adjust

Examples


# The MALAT1 dilution series stats_fit() analyses, correlated with each run's MALAT1 load:
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
result <- stats_correlate(file.path(data, "malat_dilution_log2_vs_fluc.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "malat_dilution_load_ng.tsv"))
result
#> <mzlibr_correlations> 492 features x 27 samples against malat_ng
#>   exact 4, asymptotic 308, not_estimable 180
rho <- result$records$rho
c(MALAT1 = median(rho[startsWith(result$records$feature, "MALAT1:")], na.rm = TRUE),
  FLuc = median(rho[startsWith(result$records$feature, "FLuc:")], na.rm = TRUE))
#>    MALAT1      FLuc 
#> 0.4330127 0.0000000
